WorkoutMessage.Message: Welcome to the Whoosh, 2min Capacity workout.
This is going to be a big session which culminates in you producing 2 quality efforts of 2min in duration.
But before we get to the hard work, we are going to need a good warmup first.
We are going to ease into the warmup here and gradually increase the power over the opening 3.5 minutes.
The focus of today's workout is anaerobic capacity. This is when you go well above threshold for a short period of time.
But we aren't sprinting today. We are going to produce this big power over a 2min interval.
How are those legs feeling now? Working up a sweat yet?
The first part of the workout will see you performing a couple of steady state, low intensity efforts.
Then we will briefly touch on the different intensities above threshold.
But don't worry. We give you plenty of recovery between these efforts.
That completes the first part of the warmup.
A quick rest here before we start the lower intensity steady state work.
Make sure you are drinking throughout the workout. It's important to stay hydrated.
The intensity should be pretty comfortable for you here.
Really focus on spinning the legs here. Fast legs make the effort more aerobic.
After completing the warmup, we are going to ramp up the intensity in small steps.
The end goal here is to produce 2min of top end work.
But to get there, we are going to give you a taste of each level of intensity with plenty of recovery.
And then finally, we put it all together to produce 2min of big power!
Each interval from here on in will get a little harder.
But you've got this! It's all within your abilities.
That completes the first part of the warmup. Now for an easy spin.
Just a short rest here.
Grab a drink before we step up the intensity a little.
This time we are going to complete 2min at a tempo intensity.
Again, this should be a pretty comfortable effort for you.
Concentrate on spinning the gear a little higher than what is comfortable for you.
The duration of this interval is the same as you will complete for our main set.
Obviously we are going to be going much harder in the anaerobic capacity efforts...
...but start preparing yourself for the duration of the main interval.
Nice work so far.
As the intensity increases, so does the length of our recovery intervals.
Next, we are going to step up the effort to just under your threshold power. But only for 1min.
A little harder now. But still comfortable for you.
Try to stay in the seat for these efforts and really drive the power from your glutes.
To give you an idea of what's ahead, keep in mind that our main set intervals will be 2min long and above this intensity!
Great work! This is a big session today.
Grab another drink. Everything from here on in is above threshold!
This time we are going just above threshold for the minute.
Hit that target power and really drive the pedals.
You're going to notice that your breathing rate suddenly increases in these short efforts.
That's a positive. This is where we get the training effect.
And rest again. Nice and easy here.
We have a longer recovery period this time.
How are the legs feeling? Quite often it's after the 3rd or 4th effort that the legs start to come good.
We are getting closer to the main set of work now.
Just 1 more warmup interval, then we prepare for the big ones!
This time we are going a little harder again, but just for 30sec.
It's ok to get out of the seat for this on if you prefer.
Here we go!
Hit that target power and stay on top of the gear all the way through.
There's the line... Just 10sec to go!
Nice work. That was a good effort.
Now we can really spin the legs out and have a good recovery
So far in this workout you have experienced the various levels of intensity above threshold that we are going to produce in the main set.
But this time we are going to combine them all into the 1 effort.
The target power in these intervals will gradually ramp up over the 2min.
Starting at 88% of threshold and finishing at 130%.
It's going to require a big effort, but you've got this.
Start getting yourself ready for the work ahead. We start in 20sec.
OK... Here we go!
That's a great start. Settle into a nice rhythm here.
Keep your breathing under control and try to stay relaxed.
Really drive the power from the glutes. Nice and strong here.
We are getting into the serious part now. The target power is well above threshold now.
Just 30sec to go!
Out of the seat if you need to here. There's the line!
And you're done. Great work!
That was fantastic. Catch your breath and grab a drink.
We have plenty of recovery time now.
Relax as much as you can here. Generally our cadence is a little lower during recovery after an intense interval.
In a moment we are going to repeat that interval.
Think about how the previous interval felt. Were you comfortable up to a certain point? Did it suddenly get harder?
In this next interval focus on your cadence.
Are you keeping on top of the gear by maintaining the same cadence all the way through to the end.
Start getting ready for the next effort. We go in 30sec!
Ok here we go. Let's finish off a great workout with a strong effort!
Settle into your rhythm here. Perfect start.
Control your breathing and try to stay relaxed.
Maintain your starting cadence all the way to the end. Stay on top of that gear.
You're well above threshold now. This is big power you're producing!
Just 30sec to go! C'mon.
Out of the seat if you need to here. There's the line!
And you're done. Great work!
That was a big effort from you. Well done.
We are going to take our time here and really spin the legs out to help with recovery.
You have just completed a very difficult session.
Being able to produce big power across the duration of 1 to 4min is very challenging.
It's that maximal effort that isn't quite a sprint, but it's not a long Time Trial either.
This type of training would generally only be completed once a week.
We generally need 2 or 3 days of recovery after high intensity workouts like this.
As you cool down be sure to keep drinking. It's amazing how much fluid we can lose through sweat in a 30min indoor workout.
Unlike the warmup, our cadence is generally a little lower during the cool down.
The goal of the cool down is to allow your heart rate and breathing to return to normal resting levels.
I hope you've enjoyed today's Whoosh workout. It certainly got the heart rate going.
Enjoy the rest of your cool down. Relax a little in these final moments, and we hope to see you back for more workouts on Whoosh.
